marks.gloss_en: מדקתני פתילת הבגד -- the mishna's wick is still a garment, yet R' Akiva calls it pure: so he now holds with R' Yehoshua
and R' Akiva retracted to R' Yehoshua's view
if he put it in a box, it is impure by all opinions
והא אנן יוצר תנן! -- the mishna permits only what the potter attached
מאי יוצר -- כעין יוצר: 'potter' means an attachment like a potter's, which plaster or clay provides (= p_yotzer_keein_yotzer)
the baraita: if he attached it with plaster or with potter's clay, it is permitted
the mishna: if the potter attached it from the outset, it is permitted, because it is one vessel
R' Tarfon and the elders saw us put the pierced eggshell on the lamp and said nothing (kind svara under protest: no support kind names a precedent)
אמרו לו: משם ראיה?! שאני בית נתזה דזריזין הן -- from there a proof? the house of Nitza is different, for they are vigilant

R' Yehuda: once we kept Shabbat in the upper story of the house of Nitza in Lod; we filled an eggshell with oil, pierced it and set it on the mouth of the lamp, and R' Tarfon and the elders there said nothing to us
מתיב רב יוסף: קתני קטנים -- R' Shimon's baraita includes a chair, a small item, against R' Yirmeya's 'large ones only'
מתיב רב יוסף: קתני גדולים -- R' Shimon's baraita includes a bed, a large item, which would need no permission of his if all permit large ones
R' Shimon: a person may drag a bed, a chair and a bench, provided he does not intend to make a furrow
רבי ירמיה רבה מתרץ לטעמיה: כסא דומיא דמטה -- the chair is like the bed, a large one (= p_ry_kisei_kemita)
עולא מתרץ לטעמיה: מטה דומיא דכסא -- the bed is like the chair, a small one (= p_ulla_mita_kekisei)
Ulla: the baraita's bed is like its chair -- small
Avin of Tzippori dragged a bench in a marble-floored upper story before R' Yitzchak ben Elazar
the head of the synagogue of Botzra dragged a bench before R' Yirmeya Rabba
clothing sellers [of kilayim] sell in their usual way, provided they do not intend [to be shielded] from the sun in the sun or from the rain in the rain; the modest hang them on a stick behind them
one who extinguishes the lamp because he fears gentiles or thieves, or an evil spirit, or for a sick person that he may sleep, is exempt

had it taught the eggshell only: there the Rabbis forbid, since it is not repulsive one will come to take from it; but earthenware, which is repulsive, say they agree with R' Yehuda -- so the earthenware clause teaches they forbid even that
